mainEntity.name: Does my auto insurance cover a home visit in Boca Raton?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coverage and payment depend on your policy, eligibility, medical necessity, and the circumstances of your claim. Call the office and we'll walk through what to expect before your first visit.

mainEntity.name: What if the other driver left the scene?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hit-and-run accidents can still qualify for PIP and other coverage depending on your policy. Call us and we'll help you understand your options.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a referral before a home visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — you can call directly. If you already have a police report, attorney, or other provider involved, we're happy to coordinate with them.

Florida's Personal Injury Protection (PIP) law generally requires that you receive initial medical services and care within 14 days of a car accident for the claim to remain eligible for PIP benefits. This is general information, not legal advice — waiting to see whether pain resolves on its own is one of the most common reasons Boca Raton residents miss this window.

mainEntity.name: What is an Emergency Medical Condition (EMC) and why does it matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: An Emergency Medical Condition (EMC) is a determination made by a qualifying medical provider about the severity of your injury. Under Florida PIP, this determination affects your benefit limit — up to $10,000 with an EMC diagnosis, versus $2,500 without one. Ask your insurer, your treating providers, or a qualified legal professional how this applies to your specific claim — this is general information, not legal or medical advice.
